title: FAT: Frequency-Aware Pretraining for Enhanced Time-Series Representation Learning

problem.claim: Most deep learning models work mainly with time-domain signals, constraining their ability to capture frequency-based patterns.

gap.claim: Existing frequency-aware approaches often lack generalization and require extensive domain-specific architectural adaptations.

contributions.claim: FAT is a self-supervised pretraining framework for learning generalizable frequency-aware time-series representations.
FAT uses a frequency reformer to amplify critical frequency components and enforce similarity between original and frequency-reformed representations.
FAT introduces a Knowledge-Guided Frequency Reformer to unify semantically equivalent frequency expressions and improve robustness using frequency-invariant augmented samples.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly propose FAT as a novel pretraining framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across 14 benchmark datasets and regression and classification tasks, the authors report that FAT consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance.
The authors report that FAT remains robust across diverse backbone models.
The authors report that FAT significantly outperforms existing pretraining methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frequency-domain modeling is important for time-series forecasting.
Time-domain deep learning models have limited ability to capture frequency-based patterns, while existing specialized approaches have generalization and adaptation limitations.
FAT pretrains arbitrary backbone models to extract and encode generalizable frequency patterns without inference-time architectural modifications.
Frequency reforming and knowledge-guided similarity constraints address critical frequency components, semantic equivalence, and robustness.
Experiments across 14 benchmark datasets and two task types are reported to show strong performance and robustness.

source_observation.claim: The framework pretrains generalizable frequency-aware representations for use with any backbone model and avoids inference-time architectural modifications.

interpretation.claim: Separating representation pretraining from task-specific architecture design may improve transferability across models and tasks.

application.claim: For time-series systems spanning multiple tasks or backbone architectures, consider learning reusable frequency-aware representations before task-specific training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this transferability holds outside the reported datasets, tasks, or backbone models.

source_observation.claim: Semantically equivalent time-series may have different frequency expressions, and FAT uses frequency-invariant augmented samples to address this variation.

interpretation.claim: Robust representation learning may benefit from explicitly modeling nuisance variation in frequency expression while preserving semantic similarity.

application.claim: When equivalent signals vary spectrally, use augmentations and consistency constraints designed to preserve semantic identity across frequency expressions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which frequency variations are covered or how semantic equivalence is established.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the 14 benchmark datasets.
The abstract does not provide quantitative metrics, comparison values, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the pretraining objectives, augmentation construction, or frequency reformer implementation in detail.
The abstract does not report ablation results or limitations.
